What happens to my Google / Gmail when I die?

Short answer: Google won't hand over your password. If you set up Inactive Account Manager, your chosen contacts get the data you picked after a period of inactivity. If you didn't, family can ask Google to close the account and may request some data, but Google decides case by case. Google can also delete personal accounts after 2 years of inactivity.

What to do

  1. Open myaccount.google.com → Data & privacy → 'Make a plan for your digital legacy' (Inactive Account Manager).
  2. Choose a wait period, add up to 10 trusted contacts, and pick which data each one can download.
  3. Optionally set an auto-reply and choose whether to delete the account afterwards.
  4. For a loved one who has died: use Google's deceased-user request form to ask for closure, funds or data.

Read the official policy ↗

FAQ

Can my family log into my Gmail after I die?

Not with Google's blessing. Google doesn't share passwords. Use Inactive Account Manager so contacts can download data instead.

Does Google delete inactive accounts?

Google's policy lets it delete personal accounts that have been inactive for 2 years.
